title.title: Boolean functions beat the square-root degree bound
title.subtitle: Claim: for every $C > 0$ some Boolean $f$ has $\sum_i \hat f(\{i\}) > C\sqrt{\deg f}$

plain: A yes/no rule's pull toward its inputs was thought capped by its complexity; some rules blow past any cap

beats.text: Schematic: how much can a Boolean function of degree $d$ correlate with its inputs?
Gopalan–Servedio: never more than a constant times $\sqrt d$, as majority gives
The claim: some functions beat $C\sqrt{\deg f}$ for every $C$; the true growth is open

steps: Combine independent signs into cells of low degree
Each step raises the kept variance against the degree cost
Repeat enough times and the ratio beats any constant

achievement.label: Gopalan–Servedio conjecture (c. 2009)
achievement.context: Fails for every $C > 0$; no growth rate in $n$ or the degree is given
achievement.note: Between $\sqrt d$ and $d$, the true growth is still open

verify.detail: Both the signed violation for every $C$ and the unbounded absolute ratio
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean statement; we did not build it

voice.text: Majority on d bits correlates with its inputs about root d. Was that the limit?
A gain is compounded, step by step, until it beats any constant.
Claimed: no constant times root d suffices.
